religion_note: Statistics Korea's 2015 census counted everyone from the registers and asked religion in its sample survey, which enumerated a fifth of households in the field; the answers are published weighted to the whole population (KOSIS DT_1PM1502), and the table counts 1,741,499 people here, 708,931 with a religion and 1,032,568 with none. The question is asked in the years ending in 5; KOSIS's table by district holds the 2015 round. 'Other religions' joins the table's own 기타 ('other') with Daesun Jinrihoe (1,377) and Daejongism (119), which the census counts apart.
ethnicity_note: Registered foreign residents by country of nationality at 31 December 2023 (Ministry of Justice, 시군구별 국적(지역)별 등록외국인 체류현황) against the resident-registered Korean population of the same date (Ministry of the Interior and Safety, 주민등록 인구통계): NATIONALITY, not ethnicity, which Korea's census does not ask. 'Korean' is everyone on the resident register, naturalised citizens and people of any ancestry included; 'Korean-Chinese' is the immigration statistics' own category 한국계 중국인, Chinese nationals of Korean descent, kept apart from other Chinese nationals as the Ministry lists them. Registered foreigners are those staying over ninety days who registered under the Immigration Act; overseas Koreans of foreign nationality on a domestic residence report (F-4), short-term visitors and the undocumented are not counted, so the foreign share of this province runs below the share of all foreigners present.
median_age_note: The resident register at 31 December 2025 (Ministry of the Interior and Safety): 1,779,135 registered people of this province, Korean nationals including those of unknown whereabouts and nationals abroad who keep a registration; foreigners register with the immigration office and are not counted.
